content.title: THE NEW PARENT RESET: {{SURVIVE}} THE FIRST YEAR WITHOUT WRECKING YOUR BODY
facts: **Hydrate before coffee** – drink a full glass of water before your first cup, since sleep deprivation already dehydrates you and caffeine on top makes it worse.
**Eat standing meals that count** – choose protein + fruit combos (like turkey and an apple) you can eat one-handed, so you're not running on crackers all day.
**Stretch your neck and shoulders** – 2 minutes every few hours undoes the hunch from constant feeding and carrying.
**Nap when baby naps, skip the chores** – even 20 minutes of rest lowers stress hormones more than catching up on laundry does.
**Split night wakings with a partner** – alternate who gets the first full sleep block so at least one of you gets 4+ hours uninterrupted.
**Step outside for 10 minutes daily** – fresh air and daylight reset your circadian rhythm even when your sleep schedule is chaos.
**Keep a water bottle at every feeding spot** – breastfeeding and bottle duty both spike thirst you'll otherwise ignore.
**Ask for one hour off per day** – protecting even 60 minutes for yourself prevents the burnout that builds silently in new parents.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
New parents, a few of these matter more than they sound. Hydrate before coffee is huge because sleep deprivation already pulls water from your cells, and caffeine is a mild diuretic that pulls even more — so your body ends up running on empty without you noticing the thirst signal. Stretch your neck and shoulders isn't just comfort either: constant feeding and carrying pulls your upper spine into a forward hunch, and tight muscles there are directly linked to the tension headaches so many new parents get. And stepping outside for 10 minutes daily works because morning light exposure is one of the strongest resets for your internal clock, which matters even more when your actual sleep hours are unpredictable. Everyone's body and situation is different, so adjust these to what actually fits your days.
